stem: A team moves its app from rented virtual machines to a platform service. Which task does the team stop doing?
explanation: On a platform service the provider runs and patches the operating system and runtime. Code, access decisions and data stay with the customer.
options: Protecting the data the app stores
Patching the operating system under the app
Deciding who may use the app
Writing and testing the application code

stem: A deployment script that creates hundreds of resources quickly starts failing with HTTP 429 responses from the provider API. What is the cause?
explanation: HTTP 429 means Too Many Requests. Retrying with backoff or slowing the script fixes it.
options: A missing route to the internet

stem: Moving rarely read files to the archive tier cuts the storage bill. What is the usual trade-off?
explanation: Archive storage is the cheapest to keep data in, but reads can take hours and usually cost extra.
options: Files must be deleted after one year
Slower retrieval, often with a fee to read the data
Files can no longer be encrypted

stem: What sets a community cloud apart from a public cloud?
explanation: A community cloud is shared by a defined group with common needs, such as compliance rules, while a public cloud is open to anyone.
options: It always runs in a customer's own building
Only a group of organizations with shared requirements may use it
It has no service level agreement at all

stem: Put the vulnerability management steps in order:
explanation: Set what to scan, find the weaknesses, judge their risk, then fix them and rescan to confirm.
options: Assess and rank what was found

stem: Put a typical Git change in order:
explanation: Work happens on a branch, is committed, pushed, reviewed through a pull request and then merged.
options: Push the branch to the remote
Open a pull request for review

stem: Networks, VMs and load balancers are defined in template files in Git and built from them. What practice is this?
explanation: Infrastructure as code describes resources in files that tools apply, so environments are built the same way every time.

stem: Logs from 300 servers sit on each server's local disk, and engineers log in to each one to search. What should be set up first?
explanation: Aggregation collects logs from every source into one place where they can be searched and correlated.
options: Longer local log rotation on every server

stem: A network design trusts nothing by default: every request is authenticated, authorized and checked, even from inside the corporate network. What is this approach?
explanation: Zero Trust verifies every request explicitly instead of trusting anything because of its network location.

stem: Which backup scheme makes each nightly job the smallest but needs the most backup sets for a full restore?
explanation: Each incremental holds only one day's changes, so it is small, but a restore needs the full plus every incremental since it.

stem: A company rents virtual machines on an IaaS platform. Under the shared responsibility model, who secures and patches the hypervisor that runs them?
explanation: In IaaS the provider owns the physical hosts and the virtualization layer. The customer owns the guest operating system and everything above it.

stem: A new region deployment fails with a message that the account may not launch more than 32 vCPUs of that family. What should the team do?
explanation: Accounts have service quotas. Raising the quota through the provider allows more resources.
options: Switch the VPC to a larger /16 block

stem: Many Linux servers need to mount the same directory tree at once over the network with normal file permissions. Which storage type fits?
explanation: File storage offers a shared file system over a network protocol such as NFS or SMB, so many servers can mount it together.

stem: A release reaches 5% of users first, then everyone if error rates stay low. Which strategy is this?
explanation: A canary release exposes a small share of users to the new version first to catch problems early.

stem: A scanner reports CVE-2024-3094 on several hosts. What is a CVE?
explanation: A CVE ID names one publicly disclosed vulnerability so tools and teams can refer to it the same way. CVSS is the scoring system.
options: A public identifier for a specific known vulnerability
A type of firewall rule that blocks known exploit traffic

stem: What is the purpose of a pull request?
explanation: A pull request proposes merging a branch and is where code review happens.
options: To roll back the last commit on main and push the result to everyone
To download the latest code from the remote
To have changes reviewed before merging

stem: After servers are created, a playbook in Git installs packages and sets file permissions on all of them. What practice is this?
explanation: Configuration as code defines the settings inside systems (packages, files, services) in versioned files.

stem: To find every service's log lines for one slow request, what should each service log?
explanation: Passing one trace ID along with the request and logging it everywhere ties all the entries for that request together.
options: The request's trace or correlation ID

stem: A developer has hard-coded a database password in application code stored in Git. What is the better practice?
explanation: A secrets manager keeps credentials encrypted, access-controlled, audited and rotatable, outside the code.
options: Keep it in a secrets manager fetched at run time
Email it to the team and delete it from the code afterward
Encode it in Base64 inside the code

stem: Full backup Sunday, incrementals Monday to Friday nights, failure Saturday morning. How many backup sets must be restored? Type the number only.
explanation: Restore the Sunday full and then each incremental in order, Monday through Friday: 1 + 5 = 6 sets.

stem: Code runs only when a file lands in a bucket, billed per millisecond of run time. Which service model is this?
explanation: FaaS runs event-triggered functions with no server to manage and bills per execution time.

stem: A template that worked last year now fails because it references an instance type the provider no longer offers. What is this issue?
explanation: Templates must be updated when providers retire images, instance types or API versions they reference.
options: Clock drift between the build servers

stem: One order message is delivered to billing, shipping and email services at once. What pattern is this?
explanation: Fan-out sends one event to many subscribers at the same time.

stem: A release goes onto an idle twin environment, then all traffic switches over, keeping the old one for rollback. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Blue-green keeps two full environments and switches traffic between them, so rollback is just switching back.

stem: Data about German customers stored in a German region is subject to German and EU law, wherever the company itself is based. Which concept is this?
explanation: Data sovereignty means data is governed by the laws of the country where it is stored.

stem: Every push to the repository automatically builds the code and runs the unit tests within minutes. What practice is this?
explanation: Continuous integration merges and tests changes often and automatically, catching breakage early.

stem: A firewall port opened by hand makes the live resource differ from its IaC template. What is this called?
explanation: Drift is any change to live resources made outside the code. Drift detection compares the real state with the declared state.

stem: The on-call engineer gets hundreds of alerts a day, most of them minor, and starts ignoring them. What should the team change?
explanation: Alert fatigue is fixed by triaging alerts: page only for actionable problems and route the rest to tickets or dashboards.
options: Tune alerts so only actionable ones page someone
Send every alert to more people on more channels

stem: A team wants a recognized, step-by-step configuration guide to harden its Ubuntu images. What should it use?
explanation: Center for Internet Security Benchmarks give consensus hardening settings for operating systems and cloud services.

stem: An app runs in two isolated data centers of one region to survive a site power loss. What is each data center called?
explanation: Availability zones are isolated locations inside a region with their own power and networking, used to survive a single-site failure.

stem: A service the team wants to use is available in one region but not in the region chosen for the deployment. What is the issue?
explanation: Not every service or feature exists in every region, so the design must use a region that offers it.

stem: Containers in a cluster start and stop all day and their IP addresses keep changing. How do services find each other by name?
explanation: Service discovery keeps a live registry of where each service is running, so callers look up a name instead of a fixed address.

stem: A company's only backups are snapshots kept in the same region as its VMs. Which risk remains?
explanation: Copies in the same region share its failures, so at least one copy should be kept in another region or off site.
options: Snapshots cannot be restored to a new VM
Snapshots break the RTO by design
A regional outage could take out the VMs and the backups together

stem: A web tier has 12 servers. A rolling update replaces 3 servers at a time. How many batches does the update take? Type the number only.
explanation: 12 servers divided into batches of 3 is 4 batches.

stem: After a lawsuit, legal orders that case records be kept despite the normal deletion policy. What is this?
explanation: A litigation hold suspends normal deletion for records relevant to a legal matter.

stem: A pipeline step scans dependencies for known vulnerabilities and fails the build if a critical one is found. Which pipeline concern is this?
explanation: Adding security checks to the pipeline stops vulnerable builds before they deploy.

stem: A retailer runs its store in a private cloud and sends overflow traffic to a public cloud during holiday peaks. What is this called?
explanation: Cloud bursting sends extra load from private capacity to public cloud capacity when demand spikes.

stem: A host assigned far more vCPUs than it has cores, and with every VM busy, all run slowly. What is this?
explanation: Oversubscribing CPU or memory works when VMs are mostly idle but causes contention when they are all busy.

stem: Which file format uses indentation and key: value lines, and is common for Kubernetes manifests and CI pipeline files?
explanation: YAML relies on indentation and colons. JSON uses braces, brackets and quoted keys.

stem: Which is a metric rather than a log entry?
explanation: Metrics are numeric measurements over time. Logs are records of individual events.
options: A stack trace from an exception
Average CPU use of 73% over five minutes
A record of an API call with its caller

stem: Why should containers run unprivileged instead of in privileged mode?
explanation: Privileged mode removes most isolation, so an attacker in the container can control the host.
options: A compromised privileged container can take over the host
Privileged containers cannot use the network
Unprivileged containers cannot read their own files

stem: Uploads saved in a container's writable layer vanish when the container is replaced. What should it use instead?
explanation: Data in a container's writable layer is ephemeral. A persistent volume lives outside the container and survives restarts and replacement.

stem: Database changes are copied to a standby in another region with a lag of up to five minutes. Which recovery metric does that lag mainly decide?
explanation: The lag is how much recent data could be lost in a failover, which is what the RPO measures.

stem: VMs move to the cloud unchanged so a data center can close fast. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Rehosting, often called lift and shift, moves workloads unchanged.

stem: A company has backed up nightly for two years but has never restored one. What is the main risk?
explanation: Only a test restore proves recoverability and integrity.
options: The RPO will shrink to zero
Backups may be corrupt or incomplete and nobody knows until a restore fails
Off-site copies will turn into hot sites that cost more each month
Backups will use too little storage

stem: A company wants a certification, recognized worldwide, that its information security management system meets an international standard. Which standard is it?
explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 specifies requirements for an information security management system and can be certified by an accredited body.

stem: A build produces a package to install on Red Hat Enterprise Linux servers. Which package format is it?
explanation: RHEL and related distributions use RPM packages. Debian and Ubuntu use .deb packages.

stem: Users get "server not found" for app.example.com, but the site loads when they use its IP address. What should be checked first?
explanation: Reaching the IP but not the name points to name resolution.

stem: A container listens on port 3000 inside. It is started with $\texttt{docker run -p 9000:3000 api}$. Which port do clients use on the host?
explanation: With -p host:container, port 3000 in the container is reached through host port 9000.

stem:
A deployment script contains these lines:

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{count = 3}\\\texttt{env = "prod"}\\\texttt{if env == "prod":}\\\texttt{\ \ \ \ servers = count}\\\texttt{else:}\\\texttt{\ \ \ \ servers = 1}\end{array}$$

How many web servers does it create?
explanation: env is "prod", so the condition is true and servers takes the value of count, which is 3.

stem: An online shop knows traffic triples every weekday from noon to 2 p.m. Which scaling approach fits best?
explanation: When the peak is predictable, scheduled scaling adds capacity before it arrives.
options: Scheduled scaling before noon each weekday
No scaling, with a larger cache

stem: Attackers send SQL injection strings in HTTP form fields to a public web app. Which control inspects and blocks them?
explanation: A WAF inspects HTTP requests at layer 7 and blocks patterns such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting.

stem: Match each recovery site to its description:
explanation: A hot site is fully running, a warm site needs data restored, and a cold site needs equipment brought in, so recovery time rises from hot to cold.
rows: Running copies of systems with current data, ready to take traffic almost at once
Hardware and network ready, but recent data must be loaded before use
Space and power only, with equipment to be installed after the disaster

stem: New VMs in a busy /27 subnet get no IP address, while older ones work. What is the likely cause?
explanation: A /27 has only 32 addresses before any reserved ones, so a busy subnet can run out and new VMs get no address.
options: The load balancer in front of the subnet is layer 7
The DHCP scope or subnet address space is exhausted

stem: During migration, a team packages its app into containers and runs them on the provider's managed container service, with no code changes. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations, such as a managed container platform, without rewriting the application.

stem: Admins must reach private Linux servers that have no public IP addresses. What should they connect through?
explanation: A bastion host is a hardened, monitored jump server in a public subnet that is the single entry point to private hosts.

stem: A client asks one API endpoint for exactly the fields it needs in a single query. Which technology is this?
explanation: GraphQL lets clients specify the shape of the data they want from one endpoint.

stem: A backup is restored to a new server beside the damaged one, and users move over after a check. Which recovery type is this?
explanation: A parallel recovery restores to a separate location alongside the original. An in-place recovery overwrites the original.

stem: Two virtual machines run the primary and secondary database nodes. An outage of one physical host must not take down both. Which placement rule applies?
explanation: Anti-affinity forces the two VMs onto separate hosts, so one host failure leaves the other node running. Affinity does the opposite.
options: Affinity, keeping the two together on one host
Cloning both from one shared golden template

stem: Two websites, shop.example.com and help.example.com, must share one public entry point and reach different server pools. Which load balancer can route on the Host header?
explanation: Only a layer 7 load balancer reads the HTTP Host header. A network load balancer sees only IP addresses and ports.
options: DNS round robin with health checks

stem: Peering between two VPCs fails to set up because both use 10.8.0.0/16. What is the problem?
explanation: Networks with overlapping CIDR blocks cannot be routed to each other, so one must be renumbered.
options: The VPCs are in the same region
The route tables are too small

stem: Why does a team run the same IaC template to build development, test and production?
explanation: Building every environment from one template makes them repeatable and alike.
options: So each environment gets its own hand-tuned configuration over time
So the template never needs version control
So the environments stay consistent with each other

stem: Which scaling type has no single-machine size ceiling and usually needs no restart of the servers already running?
explanation: Scaling out adds more instances alongside the running ones. Scaling up is limited by the largest instance size and often needs a restart.

stem: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
explanation: Intrusion detection watches and alerts. Intrusion prevention is inline and can drop malicious traffic.
options: An IDS blocks traffic, while an IPS only logs it
An IDS encrypts traffic at the edge, while an IPS decrypts it again inside the network
They are identical names for the same tool
An IDS detects and alerts, while an IPS sits inline and can block the traffic

stem: After a merger, one of two duplicate apps is switched off instead of moved. Which strategy applies to it?
explanation: Retiring switches off applications that are no longer needed instead of paying to move them.

stem: In SAML single sign-on to a SaaS app, which party checks the user's password and issues the signed assertion?
explanation: The identity provider authenticates the user and issues the assertion; the SaaS app, as service provider, trusts it.

stem: A live sports app pushes score changes from the server to thousands of browsers the moment they happen, over one long-lived two-way connection. Which technology fits?
explanation: WebSockets keep a persistent full-duplex connection, so the server can push updates at once.

stem: A batch job can stop and restart at any time without harm. Which billing model gives the deepest discount for it?
explanation: Spot capacity is spare capacity sold cheaply that the provider can reclaim, which suits interruptible jobs.

stem: VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B is peered with VPC C. Instances in A cannot reach C. What is the most likely reason?
explanation: Traffic cannot pass through one peering to another. A needs its own peering with C, or all three can attach to a transit gateway.
options: Route tables block all peered traffic
C and A use the same availability zone

stem:
Users intermittently get errors from a web app. The load balancer logs show:

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{status=502 target=10.0.3.14:8080 reason=connection refused}\\\texttt{status=200 target=10.0.3.15:8080}\\\texttt{status=502 target=10.0.3.14:8080 reason=connection refused}\end{array}$$

What is the most likely cause?
explanation: A 502 Bad Gateway with connection refused means the load balancer reached the target host but nothing answered on that port.
options: The client browsers are out of date
DNS is returning the wrong name for the site

stem: A vendor announces end of support for an operating system version used by 40 VMs. What does that mean for the team?
explanation: After end of support the vendor stops fixes and patches, so the systems become a growing risk.
options: The VMs will shut down on that same day
Nothing changes for the VMs until the vendor also announces end of life
The VMs will get faster updates
No more security patches will be issued, so the VMs must be upgraded or replaced

stem: A new app must keep running if one availability zone fails, at the lowest cost that meets that rule. What should be provisioned?
explanation: Spreading instances across zones meets the availability requirement, and two small instances cost less than oversizing.
options: One large instance in a single zone with nightly snapshots to another zone
Two smaller instances in two zones behind a load balancer
Two instances in the same zone
One instance with a bigger disk

stem: An autoscaling group runs 7 instances, maximum 10. Each high-CPU action adds 2. After two actions, how many run? Type the number only.
explanation: The first action takes the group from 7 to 9. The second would reach 11, but the maximum caps it at 10.

stem: An idle account's bill jumps, and several new GPU instances show 100% CPU around the clock while making outbound connections to mining pools. What is happening?
explanation: Attackers who steal credentials often launch instances to mine cryptocurrency at the victim's expense.
options: A DDoS attack against the account

stem: A company plans to build its new app around one provider's proprietary queue, database and function services. Which migration consideration does this raise most?
explanation: Heavy use of proprietary services makes a later move to another provider costly, which is vendor lock-in.

stem: Permissions are attached to job functions such as "auditor" and "operator", and users get the role that matches their job. Which model is this?
explanation: RBAC grants permissions through roles mapped to job functions.

stem: Which tool configures servers over SSH from YAML playbooks without installing an agent on them?
explanation: Ansible is agentless and pushes configuration over SSH using YAML playbooks.

stem: A team wants a relational database but does not want to patch the engine, run backups or handle failover itself. Which deployment option fits?
explanation: With a provider-managed database the provider runs patching, backups and high availability; the team manages schema and data.
options: A self-managed database on a VM
A database inside a stand-alone container
A flat file on block storage

stem: A company needs a private, consistent-bandwidth link from its data center to the cloud that does not cross the public internet. What should it order?
explanation: A dedicated connection is a private circuit to the provider. A VPN is encrypted but still rides the public internet.

stem: A scheduled scan flags that an internal API still accepts TLS 1.0 and old cipher suites. What should be done?
explanation: Deprecated protocols and ciphers have known weaknesses and should be turned off in favor of current TLS.
options: Ignore it because the API is only reachable internally
Disable the deprecated protocol versions and cipher suites

stem: Before rolling a major database engine upgrade into production, what should the team do?
explanation: Major updates can break compatibility, so they are tested in a lower environment first.
options: Upgrade only the monitoring agent first
Skip the backup to save time on the night
Apply it to production at peak hours

stem: Before an IaC change reaches production, a pipeline previews what will be created, changed or destroyed. Why?
explanation: A plan or preview step shows the effect of the code so mistakes are caught before they touch live resources.
options: To skip code review for small changes
To raise service quotas before every deployment runs
To catch unintended changes before they are applied

stem: Auditors require access logs to be kept for one year. Which logging setting enforces this?
explanation: A retention policy sets how long logs are kept before deletion.

stem: An attacker tricks a web app into requesting http://169.254.169.254/ from inside a VM and gets back temporary cloud credentials. Which attack target is this?
explanation: The instance metadata endpoint can return role credentials, so server-side request forgery against it is a known cloud attack.
options: The DHCP server for the subnet

stem: An on-premises app is moving to the cloud. Which two checks belong in the compute and platform compatibility review? (Choose two.)
explanation: Supported operating systems and CPU architecture decide whether the workload can run on the provider's compute.
options: Whether the operating system version is supported by the provider
Whether the office has enough parking
Whether the app needs a CPU architecture the provider offers
Whether staff prefer a dark theme in the console

stem: After an incident, investigators need to know which identity deleted a storage bucket and when. What provides this?
explanation: Audit logs record who did what, when and from where, which is the accounting part of identity management.
options: An audit trail of API calls

stem: Which tool builds infrastructure from declarative configuration files and keeps a state file of what it manages?
explanation: Terraform uses declarative configuration and a state file to plan and apply infrastructure changes.

stem: A block volume is provisioned at 3 IOPS for every GiB. What IOPS does a 500 GiB volume get? Type the number only.
explanation: 500 GiB x 3 IOPS per GiB = 1,500 IOPS.

stem: A service level agreement promises 99% availability over a 30-day month. How many minutes of downtime does that allow in the month? Type the number only.
explanation: A 30-day month has 30 x 24 x 60 = 43,200 minutes. One percent of that is 432 minutes.

stem: Access keys for a cloud account are found in a public code repository. What is the first thing to do?
explanation: Leaked credentials must be disabled right away, then logs reviewed for misuse.
options: Delete the repository and do nothing else
Revoke and rotate the leaked keys at once
Wait to see whether anyone used them

stem: A company subscribes to a hosted email and calendar product and only manages its users and settings. Which service model is this?
explanation: SaaS delivers a finished application; the customer manages its own data, users and settings.

stem: A deployment fails because the service account running it cannot create load balancers, though it can create VMs. What is the issue?
explanation: An access denied on one action points to missing permissions for that action.

stem: Match each dataset to the most cost-effective tier:
explanation: Constant reads belong in hot storage, occasional reads in cold storage, and records kept only for compliance in archive.
rows: Product images served to shoppers every second
Last quarter's reports opened a few times a month
Seven-year tax records kept only for audits

stem: Match each setup to its deployment model:
explanation: Your own dedicated infrastructure is private, a mix with public resources is hybrid, and a multi-tenant provider is public.
rows: Servers in your own building used only by your company
Your on-premises systems linked with resources from a public provider
Resources rented from a provider that serves many unrelated customers

stem: A CVSS 9.8 flaw is on an isolated lab VM. A CVSS 7.5 flaw on an internet-facing VPN gateway is being exploited. Which comes first?
explanation: Assessment weighs the score with exposure, exploitation and asset value, so the exposed, attacked gateway comes first.
options: Both together, because scores do not matter
The lab VM, because its score is higher
Neither, until the scores are recalculated
The VPN gateway, because exposure and active exploitation raise its real risk

stem: Two developers changed the same line in the same file on different branches. What happens when the second branch is merged?
explanation: Git cannot choose between two edits to the same line, so it marks a conflict to be resolved by hand.
options: The repository is locked for a day
A merge conflict that someone must resolve
Git keeps both lines and deletes the file
The first change is lost silently every time

stem: In JSON, which value is a list of two strings?
explanation: JSON arrays use square brackets with comma-separated values. Braces hold key-value objects.

stem: A database server is out of memory, and the database software cannot spread across several servers. Which scaling type helps?
explanation: When the software cannot run on several nodes, the fix is a bigger instance, which is vertical scaling.
options: Horizontal, adding more read-only web servers in front
Vertical, moving to an instance with more memory

stem: A function only needs to read objects from one bucket. Which permission set follows the principle of least privilege?
explanation: Least privilege grants only the actions and resources the job needs.
options: Read and write access to every bucket
Read access to that one bucket

stem: Full backup Sunday, differentials Monday to Thursday nights, failure Friday morning. How many backup sets must be restored? Type the number only.
explanation: A differential holds every change since the last full, so restore the Sunday full plus only Thursday's differential: 2 sets.

stem: A company uses a SaaS ticketing product. Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the provider?
explanation: In SaaS the provider runs and updates the whole application stack. The customer still manages users, data and its own settings.
options: Patching and updating the application itself
Setting the company's password rules in the app

stem: An app is moved to a new VM size and now runs out of memory under normal load. What is the issue?
explanation: Picking an instance smaller than the workload needs is a sizing misconfiguration.
options: A deprecated cipher suite on the load balancer

stem: A database with many small random reads and writes is slow on its current disks. Which disk type usually fixes this?
explanation: SSDs deliver far more IOPS and lower latency for random access than spinning hard disks.

stem: An app is stopped on its only server, upgraded in place and restarted. Which strategy is this?
explanation: An in-place deployment updates the existing servers directly, which usually means some downtime and a slower rollback.

stem: Match each standard or framework to what it covers:
explanation: SOC 2 is an auditor's report on controls, ISO 27001 certifies an ISMS, and the CSA publishes the Cloud Controls Matrix and the STAR registry.
rows: Audit report on a service provider's controls for security and availability
International standard for an information security management system
Cloud-specific control matrix and assurance registry

stem: Which command sends local commits to the shared remote repository?
explanation: git commit records changes locally and git push uploads them to the remote.

stem: A template change breaks production. Because the templates are in version control, what can the team do quickly?
explanation: Versioned code lets the team see what changed and roll back to a working version.
options: Turn off monitoring until the fix is found
Delete the repository and start again
Revert to the last good version
Rebuild every server by hand from memory

stem: Each time a large file lands in a bucket, processing workers are started to handle it. Which trigger is this?
explanation: Scaling in response to a specific event, such as a new file or a queue message, is event-triggered.

stem: Which protects data in transit between a browser and a cloud API?
explanation: TLS encrypts data moving over the network. Disk encryption protects data at rest.

stem: A user deleted one spreadsheet from a file share. What kind of restore fits best?
explanation: Granular recovery brings back individual items without overwriting everything else.
options: A granular restore of that single file
A failover to the DR region
Rebuilding the file server from scratch
A bulk restore of the whole volume

stem: Match each offering to its service model:
explanation: Virtual machines are IaaS, a managed runtime is PaaS, and a finished application is SaaS.
rows: Renting virtual machines and attaching your own disks and networks
Deploying code to a managed runtime that patches itself
Using a finished customer relationship management product in a browser

stem: A provider status page shows that its object storage service is down in one zone but working in others. Which kind of outage is this?
explanation: When only some zones or features fail, the outage is partial.

stem: Which object storage feature keeps earlier copies of an object when it is overwritten or deleted, so a mistake can be undone?
explanation: With versioning on, each overwrite or delete keeps the previous version, which can be restored.

stem: Instances behind a load balancer are updated a few at a time, while the rest keep serving traffic. Which strategy is this?
explanation: A rolling deployment updates instances in batches so capacity stays up throughout.
options: In-place on every server at once

stem: Records are labeled public, internal, confidential or restricted so each label gets the right controls. What is this?
explanation: Classification sorts data by sensitivity so protection matches risk.

stem: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
explanation: Continuous delivery stops at a release-ready artifact that someone approves. Continuous deployment pushes it to production automatically.
options: Delivery skips testing, while deployment runs tests
Delivery keeps every build ready to release with a manual approval, while deployment releases every passing build automatically
They are two names for the same process
Deployment only builds container images for the cluster, while delivery only builds virtual machine images for the hypervisor

stem: In a template, which data type fits the value 443 for a listener port?
explanation: A whole number such as a port is an integer.

stem: Over several weeks, traffic has grown steadily by about 5% a week. Which trigger uses this pattern to add capacity ahead of demand?
explanation: Trending-based scaling uses the growth pattern over time to forecast and add capacity before limits are reached.

stem: A scan finds an object storage bucket of customer exports that anyone on the internet can list and read. What is the right fix?
explanation: Public storage must be closed with access controls. Hiding the name is not a control.
options: Rename the bucket to something long and hard to guess
Move the files into a deeper folder
Block public access and grant only needed readers

stem: A factory processes camera images on servers beside the line to decide within milliseconds. What is this?
explanation: Edge computing moves processing close to where data is created to cut latency.

stem: Match each HTTP status code to its meaning:
explanation: 401 means credentials are missing or invalid, 403 means the identity is known but lacks permission, and 503 means the service cannot handle the request right now.

stem: Why do architects put a message queue between an order service and an inventory service?
explanation: A queue decouples the two: messages wait until the consumer is ready, so failures and spikes are absorbed.
options: So both services must always run together on the same physical host with shared memory
So the order service no longer needs any storage
So the two are loosely coupled and one can fail without stopping the other
So the inventory service can skip authentication

stem: Backups are written to object storage in another region. What protects their contents if the bucket is ever exposed?
explanation: Encryption keeps backup data unreadable without the key, wherever it is stored.

stem: A site serves 40,000 requests an hour, and a canary gets 5% of them. How many an hour reach the canary? Type the number only.
explanation: 5% of 40,000 is 40,000 x 0.05 = 2,000 requests an hour.

stem: A customer contract says the provider must keep transaction records for five years. Which kind of retention is this?
explanation: Retention required by an agreement between parties is contractual. Retention required by law is regulatory.

stem: Where should a pipeline keep the versioned packages and images it builds so later stages and environments use the same files?
explanation: An artifact repository stores build outputs with versions, so the exact tested artifact is what deploys.

stem: A company replaces its cold site with a hot site. Which recovery metric improves the most?
explanation: A hot site is already running, so service is back far sooner, which shortens the recovery time.

stem: Users report that tokens are rejected as expired the moment they are issued, but only on one server. What should be checked?
explanation: Token checks depend on time. A server clock drifting from NTP makes valid tokens look expired or not yet valid.
options: That server's clock and NTP sync

stem: A script needs the same tagging steps for every resource type. What should the repeated steps become?
explanation: Putting repeated logic in a function avoids copy and paste and keeps changes in one place.
options: A new variable for each tag
A function called for each resource
A second copy of the script for each resource type

stem: Each instance serves 500 requests a second. Six run, and demand will reach 4,200. How many more are needed? Type the number only.
explanation: 4,200 / 500 = 8.4, so 9 instances are needed. With 6 running, 3 more are needed.

stem: A public API is hammered by one client making thousands of calls a second. Which control protects the back end?
explanation: Rate limits cap requests per client so one caller cannot overwhelm the service.
options: Rate limiting and throttling at the API gateway
A larger CDN cache in every region

stem: Where do build pipelines store versioned container images so clusters can pull them at deploy time?
explanation: An image registry stores and serves container images by name and tag.

stem: Backups are copied to another region every six hours. The business sets an RPO of two hours. What is the problem?
explanation: The worst case loses everything since the last copy, up to six hours, which is longer than the two-hour RPO.
options: Copying to another region breaks the RPO by design
Recovery would take six hours to finish, which misses the RTO
Nothing, because six-hour copies meet a two-hour RPO
Up to six hours of data could be lost, which misses the RPO

stem: A monolithic app cannot scale, so the team rebuilds it as microservices on managed container and function services. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Re-architecting changes the application's structure to use cloud-native services, which costs the most effort and gains the most.

stem: A team replicates its database to another region in near real time and believes it no longer needs backups. What is the flaw?
explanation: A dropped table or ransomware encryption replicates within seconds. Backups give earlier points to go back to.
options: Replication copies deletions too, so backups are still needed
Replication encrypts data with its own key, so the copy cannot be restored later
Replication is always slower than backups

stem: Besides a password, administrators must approve a push notification on their phone. What is this?
explanation: MFA combines something you know with something you have or are.

stem: Match each description to the web service style:
explanation: REST uses resources and HTTP verbs, SOAP uses XML envelopes and contracts, and RPC invokes remote procedures.
rows: Resources at URLs acted on with standard HTTP verbs
XML envelopes with a strict contract, often described by WSDL
Calling a function on a remote server as if it were local

stem: Instances in a private subnet cannot download updates from the internet, though public instances can. What is most likely missing?
explanation: Private instances reach the internet outbound only through NAT, which needs a route in their route table.
options: A second availability zone with its own subnets
A route to a NAT gateway

stem: A team runs dozens of containers across many hosts and needs automatic restarts, scaling and rolling updates. What does it need?
explanation: An orchestrator schedules containers across hosts, restarts failed ones and handles scaling and updates.
options: Stand-alone containers started by hand on one host

stem: Why should an IaC module include a README listing its inputs, outputs and an example?
explanation: Documentation explains how to use the code, which makes reuse safer.
options: So the tool skips drift detection for that module entirely
So other teams can reuse it correctly
So it no longer needs testing in the pipeline
So it runs faster on every apply

stem: Match each need to the observability signal:
explanation: Logs hold event details, metrics hold numbers over time, and traces follow a request through services.
rows: See the error message and stack trace from one failed request
Watch memory use trend over the last month
Find which downstream call slowed a request

stem: Match each control to its job:
explanation: DLP finds and blocks sensitive data leaving, DDoS protection absorbs attack traffic, and endpoint protection guards individual machines.
rows: Stops employees from emailing files full of card numbers out of the company
Absorbs floods of traffic aimed at taking a site offline
Detects malware on a server or laptop

stem: What is a common drawback of running workloads across several public cloud providers?
explanation: Multicloud reduces dependence on one provider but adds different consoles, services and skills to manage.
options: No way to avoid any single provider outage
Data can never leave the first provider
Every workload must run in one region
More tools, skills and management overhead

stem: After a change, traffic to an on-premises network 172.16.0.0/16 goes out the internet gateway and fails. What is the issue?
explanation: Without a specific route to the on-premises range, the default route sends it to the internet.
options: A spot instance being reclaimed by the provider in the middle of the transfer
A missing route to the on-premises link

stem: A mainframe system has a strict regulatory reason to stay in the company's data center for now. What does the migration plan do with it?
explanation: Retaining keeps a workload where it is, at least for now, often for compliance, cost or timing reasons.

stem: Which sign-in protocol, built on OAuth 2.0, gives a mobile app an ID token describing the user?
explanation: OpenID Connect adds an identity layer and ID tokens on top of OAuth 2.0's authorization flows.

stem: A sign-up publishes a message, and separate services react on their own to email and bill the user. What architecture is this?
explanation: In event-driven systems, producers publish events and consumers react independently.

stem: Which change is usually a minor update rather than a major one?
explanation: Minor updates fix bugs and add small improvements with backward compatibility. Major versions can break things.
options: A patch release that fixes bugs without changing features
A move to a new database engine
A new major version that removes an old API
A full rewrite of the user interface and its settings

stem: A machine learning VM needs direct access to a physical GPU for near-native performance. What feature provides it?
explanation: Pass-through hands a physical device such as a GPU straight to a VM instead of emulating it.

stem: Fifty VPCs and two on-premises sites all need to reach each other without building a full mesh of peering links. What fits best?
explanation: A transit gateway is a hub that each network attaches to once, so routing does not need a link for every pair.
options: A peering link between every pair

stem: A host carries VLANs 10 and 20, but VLAN 20 VMs are cut off. Its switch port is an access port in VLAN 10. What is wrong?
explanation: An access port carries one untagged VLAN. A host with several VLANs needs a trunk port that passes tagged traffic.
options: The VMs need public IP addresses
The port must be a trunk port
The host needs more memory for the VMs on VLAN 20

stem: A deployment asks for 4 replicas, each requesting 2 vCPUs. How many vCPUs in total? Type the number only.
explanation: 4 replicas x 2 vCPUs each = 8 vCPUs.

stem: An app writes 20 GB of logs a day, kept for 90 days. How many GB are stored at most? Type the number only.
explanation: 20 GB a day x 90 days = 1,800 GB.

stem: Which control filters traffic at the virtual NIC or subnet with port and address rules, and is stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically?
explanation: Security groups are stateful packet filters attached to instances or subnets.

stem: A company moves a workload from one public provider to another after a pricing change. Which migration type is this?
explanation: Moving between two cloud providers is a cloud-to-cloud migration.

stem: A photo printing site asks to read a user's cloud photo album without ever seeing the user's password. Which framework grants that limited access?
explanation: OAuth 2.0 lets a user grant an app scoped access tokens to a resource without sharing credentials.

stem: Match each tool to its main job:
explanation: Jenkins runs CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes orchestrates containers, and Grafana builds dashboards.
rows: Automating build and test pipelines with jobs and a Jenkinsfile
Running and scaling containers across a cluster
Showing metrics from many sources on dashboards

stem: Finance cannot tell which department caused a cloud bill spike. What should be applied to every resource?
explanation: Tags label resources so the bill can be grouped and charged back by department or project.
options: Tags for department and cost center
A separate overlay network for each team

stem: Users across five continents complain that large static images load slowly from a single region. What should be added?
explanation: A CDN caches static content at edge locations close to users, cutting load time.

stem: A developer with read-only rights uses a misconfigured role to grant themselves administrator access. What is this?
explanation: Gaining higher rights than intended is privilege escalation, often through overly broad permissions on roles.

stem: A team decommissions an application. Which step matters most for the data it held?
explanation: Decommissioning includes handling data under retention rules and securely removing what is no longer needed.
options: Stop billing alerts for the account
Leave the volumes attached to a stopped VM in case someone finds them useful later
Handle the data under the retention policy and wipe the rest

stem: A workload stores payment card data. Which requirement must drive where and how its resources are provisioned?
explanation: Card data brings compliance rules on encryption, access and network separation that the build must meet.
options: The cheapest region regardless of rules
Compliance requirements such as PCI DSS

stem: An alert fires that disk space on a database volume is at 92%. What is the right first response?
explanation: Triage confirms and sizes the problem before the response, so the fix is safe and in proportion.
options: Ignore it until the disk is full
Restart every server in the region
Triage it: confirm it, size the impact, then act
Delete the database's oldest table at once

stem: An HTTPS-only web server also listens to the internet on TCP 3306 and 6379. What is the finding?
explanation: Ports 3306 (MySQL) and 6379 (Redis) should never face the internet on a web server; they should be closed.
options: A DDoS attack in progress against the web server

stem: Customer data from an EU subsidiary must stay inside the EU after migration. Which consideration is this?
explanation: Laws on where personal data may be stored and processed are regulatory considerations that limit which regions can be used.

stem: A script running on a build server creates cloud resources. How should it authenticate?
explanation: Automation uses programmatic credentials through the API, SDK or CLI, scoped to only what it needs.
options: Programmatic access with a scoped API key or role, not a person's console password
With no authentication on a private network
With an administrator's web portal login and password saved in the script for convenience
Through RDP to a jump box

stem: In the ELK stack, which component collects and transforms log data before it is stored?
explanation: Logstash ingests and processes logs, Elasticsearch stores and indexes them, and Kibana visualizes them.

stem: A licence is priced per physical CPU core and its terms forbid sharing hardware with other customers. Which billing option fits?
explanation: A dedicated host gives you a whole physical server, so per-core licences can be counted and the hardware is not shared.

stem: A dedicated link to the cloud has a VPN backup, and routes must fail over on their own. Which protocol exchanges them?
explanation: BGP advertises routes between networks and withdraws them when a link fails, so traffic shifts to the remaining path.

stem: An inventory finds a remote access tool on several VMs that no one approved or installed through the normal process. What is the issue?
explanation: Software installed outside the approved process is unauthorized and may be a sign of compromise.

stem: A container writes temporary cache files that can be rebuilt at any time. Which kind of data is this?
explanation: Ephemeral data can be lost without harm when the container or instance goes away.

stem: A declarative IaC tool is run twice with no change to the code. What should the second run do?
explanation: Declarative tools are idempotent: they change only what differs from the desired state.
options: Create a second copy of every resource it declared
Delete everything and rebuild it from scratch
Make no changes, since nothing differs
Ignore the state file and guess

stem: A team wants to know when its public website stops answering, even if every server looks healthy from inside. What should it add?
explanation: External checks test what users see, which catches DNS, certificate and network problems internal metrics can miss.
options: More debug logging on the web servers

stem: A test VM built two years ago for a demo is still running, unpatched and unmonitored, with a public IP. What is this risk called?
explanation: Forgotten, unmanaged instances are zombie instances: they cost money and give attackers an easy target.

stem: An analytics cluster moves from the cloud back into the company's own data center to cut costs. Which migration type is this?
explanation: Bringing a workload back from a provider into your own facility is a cloud-to-on-premises migration.

stem: Fifty data analysts need the same read-only access to a warehouse. What is easiest to manage?
explanation: Group-based access control grants permissions once to a group, so joiners and leavers are handled by membership.
options: Put them in a group and grant the access to the group
Grant each analyst the same access one person at a time

stem: Where are GitHub Actions workflows defined?
explanation: GitHub Actions reads YAML workflow files stored in the repository's .github/workflows folder.
options: In a Jenkinsfile on a separate build server
In the Docker registry next to the images it builds

stem: How many hours does copying 900 GB over a steady 1 Gbps link take, ignoring overhead? Type the number only.
explanation: 900 GB is 900 x 8 = 7,200 gigabits. At 1 gigabit per second that takes 7,200 seconds, which is 2 hours.

stem: How many IP addresses does the block 10.40.0.0/19 contain in total, before reserved ones? Type the number only.
explanation: A /19 leaves 32 - 19 = 13 host bits, and 2 to the 13th power is 8,192 addresses.

stem: App servers wait 180 ms per round trip to a database on another continent, so chatty queries crawl. What is the main issue?
explanation: Every round trip pays the cross-continent delay, so moving the database closer or batching queries helps.
options: A misconfigured VLAN tag on the trunk

stem: Which object decides where traffic leaving a subnet is sent next, for example to an internet gateway or a VPN?
explanation: Each subnet is associated with a route table whose entries map destination ranges to targets.

stem: A support team wants to know whether incoming customer reviews are positive or negative, using a managed AI service. Which capability fits?
explanation: Sentiment analysis classifies the tone of text as positive, negative or neutral.

stem: Match each risk profile to the strategy that fits it best:
explanation: Blue-green rolls back by switching environments, canary tests with a small share of users, and rolling updates a few servers at a time.
rows: Must roll back in seconds by switching traffic
Wants real users to test the release on a small scale first
Has spare capacity for only a few servers at a time

stem: Match each snippet to its format:
explanation: Braces and quoted keys are JSON, key: value lines are YAML, and tags are XML.
rows: {"size": "small"}
size: small
<size>small</size>

stem: An administrator adds two instances by hand before a planned product launch. Which scaling approach is this?
explanation: Changing capacity by hand is manual scaling.

stem: Match each backup type to what it captures:
explanation: Full copies all data, incremental copies changes since the latest backup, and differential copies changes since the last full.
rows: Everything selected, every time
Changes since the last backup of any kind
Changes since the last full backup

stem: A regulator requires that health records physically stay on servers inside the country. Which concept is this requirement about?
explanation: Data locality is where the data physically resides.

stem: A service account that normally makes 50 API calls a day makes 9,000 calls from a new country overnight. What should flag this?
explanation: Comparing activity to the normal baseline catches unusual behavior that may be a compromise.

stem: A company's base container images contain internal tools that must not be shared outside. Where should they be stored?
explanation: Private repositories restrict who can pull internal artifacts.
options: A shared download link with no login

stem: Large file transfers between two regions are slow, though small requests return quickly. Which issue fits best?
explanation: Fast small requests but slow large transfers point to limited throughput rather than latency or resolution.

stem: Which service checks the identity and rules of web traffic before it reaches the application servers, often adding TLS termination and URL routing in one place?
explanation: An application gateway is a layer 7 entry point that routes and inspects HTTP traffic for back-end servers.

stem: Farm sensors send readings to a local device that batches them for the cloud. What is that device?
explanation: An IoT gateway collects data from nearby sensors, often over short-range protocols, and relays it to the cloud.

stem: Which migration strategy rewrites much of the application's code to use cloud features, without necessarily redesigning the whole architecture?
explanation: Refactoring changes the code itself, for example to use managed services or stateless sessions.

stem: In a script, the line max_nodes = 10 does what?
explanation: A single equals sign assigns a value. A double equals sign compares.
options: Assigns the value 10 to a variable

stem: Which step of logging installs agents or uses provider services to gather log data from each source?
explanation: Collection gathers logs at the source. Aggregation then centralizes them and retention decides how long they stay.

stem: A business sets an RPO of one hour for its order database. How often must backups or snapshots run at least?
explanation: The backup interval must be no longer than the RPO, or more data than allowed could be lost.

stem: Which two protocols do administrators commonly use to manage cloud VMs directly? (Choose two.)
explanation: SSH and RDP give remote shells and desktops. SMTP sends mail and NTP keeps time.

stem: Files on several shared drives are encrypted and a note demands payment for the key. What attack is this?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts data and demands payment for the decryption key.

stem: Which tool packages an application and its dependencies into an image and runs it as a container?
explanation: Docker builds images and runs containers from them.

stem: A client supports only HTTP/1.1, and the server accepts only a newer protocol. What is this issue?
explanation: Both ends must share a supported protocol version.

stem: A company wants the lowest recovery time and is willing to pay for it. Which two choices support that? (Choose two.)
explanation: A running hot site and continuous replication shorten both the outage and the data loss. Cold sites and weekly tapes are cheap but slow.
options: Keep a hot site running in a second region
Replicate data continuously to the recovery site
Ship backup tapes weekly to a vault
Rely on a cold site with no servers

stem: Monitoring shows a VM sized for 16 vCPUs never uses more than 3. What should the team do to save money?
explanation: Rightsizing matches the instance size to real use, cutting cost without hurting performance.
options: Buy a reserved instance of the same size
Rightsize it to a smaller instance
Move it to a dedicated host

stem: Before cutover, a team checks that the target region has enough vCPU quota and storage for every migrated workload. Which planning step is this?
explanation: Resource allocation makes sure the target has the compute, storage and network capacity the workloads need.

stem: A reporting job runs only at night and can tolerate interruption. Which requirement should guide its compute choice most?
explanation: A flexible night job is best matched on cost, for example with spot capacity or scheduled shutdown.

stem: A web tier scales out when CPU passes 70%. Which two settings stop it from adding and removing instances over and over? (Choose two.)
explanation: Cooldowns and a gap between scale-out and scale-in thresholds prevent flapping.
options: A cooldown period after each scaling action

stem: A cloud provider says an instance type reaches end of life next quarter. What should the team plan?
explanation: At end of life the offering is withdrawn, so workloads must move before it disappears.
options: Moving the workloads to a current instance type before that date
Turning off monitoring for those instances
Buying more of that instance type
Nothing, because end of life only changes how the instances are billed each month

stem: After signing in once, an API client sends a signed, time-limited bearer token with each call instead of a password. Which authentication model is this?
explanation: Token-based authentication issues a token after sign-in that the client presents on later requests until it expires.

stem: Which two actions harden a new VM image? (Choose two.)
explanation: Hardening shrinks the attack surface and starts from a patched baseline.
options: Open all ports for easier troubleshooting
Apply current patches before saving the image
Enable the default administrator account with a shared password

stem: A team keeps main always deployable and does all work on short-lived branches that are merged after review. What is this?
explanation: A branching strategy controls how work is isolated and merged into main.

stem: A provider announces that an old API version will stop working, and scripts that call it start failing after the date. What is this issue?
explanation: Deprecated features are removed after notice, so code must move to the replacement.

stem: Which load balancer forwards TCP and UDP traffic by IP address and port with very low latency, without reading the HTTP content?
explanation: A network load balancer works at layer 4, so it is fast and handles any TCP or UDP protocol, but it cannot route on URLs.

stem: Which two are non-relational database types? (Choose two.)
explanation: Document and key-value stores are NoSQL models. Normalized tables and star schemas are relational designs.

stem: Which deployment model runs on infrastructure dedicated to one organization, whether in its own building or hosted for it?
explanation: A private cloud serves a single organization, on premises or hosted.

stem: A linter flags a syntax error in a template before anything is deployed. What kind of check is this?
explanation: Validation and linting check the code itself before it runs against real resources.
options: A penetration test by an outside firm

stem: Which alert should page an engineer at 3 a.m.?
explanation: Pages are for customer-facing, actionable problems. The others are informational.
options: A development VM used 60% CPU for most of the afternoon
The checkout service is returning errors to customers
A weekly report finished on time

stem: A restore test checks that file hashes match the originals. Which property is being tested?
explanation: Matching hashes show the restored data is unchanged, which is integrity.

stem: A company's cloud accounts check users against its existing Active Directory instead of separate cloud-only accounts. Which model is this?
explanation: Directory-based authentication uses a central directory service as the source of identities.

stem: An employee enters cloud console credentials on a fake login page sent by email. Which attack type is this?
explanation: Phishing is social engineering that tricks a person into giving up credentials.

stem: Which two are archive formats a pipeline might produce as flat artifacts? (Choose two.)
explanation: ZIP and tar bundle files into one archive. SAML is an identity standard and CVE names vulnerabilities.

stem: A user can open files in a storage bucket that their team should never see. Which two should be reviewed? (Choose two.)
explanation: Unauthorized access comes from permissions on the resource or on the identity, so both need review.
options: The user's role and group memberships
The bucket policy and access control settings
